title: A stabilised carbanion: the enolate
caption: A carbanion is a negatively charged carbon. Most are very reactive, but one next to a C=O is stabilised because its charge is delocalised onto the oxygen. The two resonance forms of propanone's enolate differ only in where the electrons are drawn.
alt: Two resonance structures of the propanone enolate joined by a double-headed arrow: charge on carbon, and charge on oxygen.
description: Left: the negative charge on the CH₂ carbon next to C=O.
Right: the same ion with C=C and the negative charge on oxygen, the more important form.
